The U.S. Army said it is pushing through with the controlled detonation of more than five dozen barrels of a toxic explosive chemical in an Iowa munitions plant on Wednesday, despite public outcry over the potential health impacts on neighboring communities and an ongoing legal battle. Nearly five tons of degraded lead azide, a chemical compound used as a detonator in cartridges and shells, are set to be detonated at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, a …
